defs: Internet of Things: network-connected devices such as sensors, appliances, cameras, and embedded devices.

slides.title: IoT Components
slides.raw:
IoT Components
• Sensors and Actuators
• Connectivity
• Data Processing
• Cloud Computing
• User Interface
slides.teach: Know what each component does and how the components work together. CompTIA often asks which component best fits a scenario.
defs: Computing resources delivered on demand from a provider rather than entirely owned and operated locally.
Internet of Things: network-connected devices such as sensors, appliances, cameras, and embedded devices.

course.learn: Internet of Things (IoT) devices are network-connected sensors, appliances, controllers, and embedded devices that often have limited resources, long lifecycles, weak defaults, or inconsistent update support.
course.why: Poorly secured IoT can become an entry point or botnet participant.
course.example: Security cameras ship with default passwords and are placed on a dedicated VLAN with outbound restrictions and monitoring.
course.exam: Common mitigations: change defaults, patch, inventory, disable unused services, segment IoT, and monitor unusual behavior.

breakdown.explanation: Physical sensors detect environmental or movement conditions that may indicate intrusion or danger. Different sensors detect heat, pressure, microwave reflection, sound, motion, moisture, or other changes.
Secure architecture depends on where devices are placed, which trust zones they belong to, how they connect, what attack surface they expose, and what happens when a component fails.
